Amazon Transportation Services（ATS）は、お客様にお約束したお届け日を正確に守るため、日本全国の輸送ネットワークを統括する部門です。 ATSの重要な組織のひとつがRelay Operation Center（ROC）です。ROCは24時間365日体制で輸送ネットワークを管理し、オペレーションをサポートしています。 ROCは複数の専門チームで構成されており、それぞれが輸送ネットワークの異なる側面を担当しています。その中でも、物流倉庫・配送拠点のオペレーション品質と効率性を直接支えるのが、Transportation Operation Management（TOM）チームです。

TOMチームは日本全国の物流倉庫・配送拠点における安全性、品質、生産性の向上を支援するチームです。 私たちは、単にデータを監視するだけではありません。現場で実際に何が起きているのかを理解し、拠点の担当者と協働しながら、実効性のある改善を実現することを大切にしています。

TOMチームが担う3つの領域

1. 品質管理 物流倉庫・配送拠点において定められたオペレーションプロセスが正確に実施され安全や品質が担保されているかを確認します。

2. 資材管理 配送に不可欠な資材（カート他）の在庫を全国規模で管理しています。各拠点に必要な数量を適切に配置し、不足や過剰在庫を防ぐことで、スムーズな配送オペレーションを支えています。

3. プロセス改善 日々のオペレーションから得られるデータを分析し、業務プロセスの標準化・効率化を推進します。

物流未経験からキャリアアップ可能なポジションです。私達と一緒に新たにAmazonの歴史を作り上げましょう！

現在は当たり前となった「お急ぎ便」「お届け日時指定便」「当日便」は、お客様の利便性を追求し実現した、日本発の配送サービスです。そのサービスを実現しているのはアマゾンの心臓部である物流拠点、フルフィルメントセンター（以下FC）の仕組みにあります。

FCはお客様のご注文に対して、より早く正確に商品を、多くの地域へ提供するため、入荷から出荷までの各工程において、Amazon独自のノウハウを活かした効率的かつ的確な管理を実施し、最新の自社テクノロジーを導入する事で更なる最適化に挑戦し続けている事業です。

そのFC事業は、日本で2005年に開業して以来、現在25拠点以上に成長しました。本年も継続して事業の拡大に伴い、私達と一緒にお客様起点に考え、更なるイノベーションを起こしていただける情熱的な仲間を「プロセスアシスタント」として募集します。

「プロセスアシスタント」には、他業種・職種も含めこれまでの経験、スキルを活かし、改善点を模索しながら、より便利でお客様に満足いただける高い品質のサービスを提供できるビジネスをつくる事、そして先進テクノロジーと「People First」の考え方で、安全・快適・楽しい職場環境の構築を行う、将来の組織のリーダーを目指していただける事を期待しています。

AWS のクラウド技術はお客様のフィードバックやご要望に基づき日々進化を続けています。そのため、入社後も最新技術やトレンドを学び続けることが必要不可欠です。このポジションに応募する時点では AWS やクラウド技術を身につけていることは必須ではありません。継続的なスキルアップの一環として、入社後にクラウドに関する知識を身につけようとする意欲を重視します。

Overview

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day. Microsoft Cloud Operations and Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than one hundred datacenters and one million servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts, who work tirelessly to support digital services for more than one billion customers and twenty million businesses in over ninety countries worldwide.

Within CO+I, the Core Datacenter Services (CDS) team is responsible for improving the availability, resilience, and efficiency of Microsoft’s global cloud infrastructure. We are seeking a Senior Director, MRO Supply Chain - Datacenter Operations to lead the end-to-end supply chain for maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) spare parts supporting datacenters globally. Additionally, this role has responsibility for destruction equipment strategy and qualification that includes the spare part planning and fulfilment of maintenance standards within our datacenters and circular centers. This senior leader will set the vision, operating model, and transformation agenda for the function, building the capabilities, systems, partnerships, and talent required to plan, source, position, move, replenish, repair, recover, and manage critical spare parts throughout their lifecycle. The role is accountable for supply and demand planning, logistics, warehousing, supply network design, inventory strategy, supplier execution, and service performance in support of reliable datacenter operations and Microsoft’s AI and cloud growth.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities
  • Set and communicate the global end-to-end MRO spare-parts supply chain vision, strategy, standards, and multi-year transformation roadmap, aligned to CO+I priorities, datacenter reliability, AI capacity growth, company goals, financial objectives, and customer commitments.
  • Lead, develop, and inspire a geographically distributed organization of supply chain professionals and leaders. Establish clear accountability, strengthen succession and talent pipelines, coach and mentor team members and leaders, and create an inclusive, high-performance culture with efficient processes through significant change.
  • Own end-to-end supply chain performance for MRO spare parts across demand and supply planning, sourcing and supplier execution, inventory management, warehousing, transportation and logistics, supply network design, deployment, returns, repair loops, recovery, and end-of-life disposition.
  • Develop and execute supply-planning targets and replenishment standards across all nodes in the supply chain. Deliver measurable improvement in availability, On Time in Full (OTIF), inventory turns, excess and obsolescence, expedite cost, and total cost to serve.
  • Ensure inventory is available at the right place, at the right time, and at the right cost, expertly balancing business and customer needs to protect datacenter uptime and provide seamless customer experiences.
  • Design and optimize the global supply network, including stocking locations, replenishment flows, service levels, lead-time strategies, transportation models, and resilience measures. Balance availability, risk, cost, sustainability, and working capital.
  • Lead day-to-day and strategic relationships with third parties, suppliers, and logistics partners to ensure safety, security, quality, resilience, compliance, capacity, and service performance while maximizing execution and driving continuous improvement.
  • Escalate and resolve field supply chain issues; prioritize service based on material lead times, criticality, and availability; analyze material consumption trends; review engineering change orders affecting spare parts; and ensure hardware compatibility and lifecycle readiness.
  • Define risk-based strategies for critical spares, long-lead components, lifecycle transitions, repair and return loops, substitutions, constrained supply, and excess and obsolete inventory.
  • Implement measurement frameworks and performance-management mechanisms that enable data-driven decision-making, evaluate business and supplier performance, identify optimization opportunities, and provide clear ownership and disciplined execution.
  • Serve as the executive expert in the tools and processes used to manage supply. Lead the transformation of processes, data, governance, and digital capabilities through automation, integrated systems, advanced analytics, scenario planning, and scalable inventory solutions.
  • Define and drive process changes, standardization, and maturity improvements. Lead complex change-management efforts, influence teams to adopt new ways of working, and collaborate cross-functionally to improve tools, processes, and service delivery.
  • Build executive-level relationships across Sourcing, Finance, Datacenter Operations, Engineering, Security, Sustainability, regional teams, suppliers, and other disciplines. Resolve complex trade-offs, influence investment decisions, and align stakeholders behind enterprise priorities.
  • Ensure supply chain operations meet Microsoft safety, security, regulatory, and business-continuity requirements, with safe and secure solutions for internal and external customer commitments as the highest priority.
  • Represent the function with senior executives and external partners, clearly communicating strategy, investment needs, risks, performance, transformation progress, and business outcomes.
  • Embody our culture and values.

    Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Additional or Preferred Qualifications
  • Bachelor's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Supply Chain or related field AND 15+ years supply planning, operations, supply chain, indirect supply planning, technology-related supply chain, sourcing and manufacturing, Sales & Operations Planning, material requirement planning systems and tools, quantitative & qualitative analysis in cross functional or organizational enterprise environment, or related experience OR Master's Degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Supply Chain Analytics, or related field AND 12+ years supply planning, operations, supply chain, indirect supply planning, technology-related supply chain, sourcing and manufacturing, Sales & Operations Planning, material requirement planning systems and tools, quantitative & qualitative analysis in cross functional or organizational enterprise environment, or related experience OR equivalent experience.
  • Demonstrated experience leading leaders and large, geographically distributed, cross-functional teams through significant organizational, process, and technology transformation.
  • Deep functional expertise across supply and demand planning, logistics, inventory management, and supply network design, with a record of improving service, resilience, cost, and working capital at scale.
  • Significant experience managing MRO materials, service parts, or mission-critical spare-parts supply chains in datacenter, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, utilities, industrial, manufacturing, aerospace, healthcare, or a similarly complex and uptime-sensitive environment.
  • Proven ability to define strategy, translate it into an executable operating model and roadmap, secure investment, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
  • Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with experience aligning senior stakeholders and resolving complex priorities across operations, engineering, sourcing, finance, and suppliers.
  • Experience establishing governance, metrics, and management systems for end-to-end supply chain performance, risk, and accountability.
  • Experience redesigning supply networks and deploying integrated planning, inventory, warehouse, transportation, and analytics capabilities at enterprise scale.
  • Working knowledge of cloud or datacenter infrastructure, including the operational dependencies associated with power, cooling, space, racks, cabling, and hardware maintenance.

Overview

Microsoft Advertising is the destination for experienced, collaborative and passionate digital advertising professionals seeking a rewarding career. We offer a compelling portfolio of advertising products, innovative solutions and the opportunity to work with talented people across the digital advertising industry. 

We are seeking a Service Engineering Manager to lead a team of Service and Automation Engineers providing advanced technical support for the Microsoft Advertising business while building scalable engineering solutions that improve customer outcomes, service reliability and operational efficiency. The role will support advertising experiences delivered through Microsoft Advertising and partner publisher sites. 

This role combines people leadership, service engineering and technical strategy. You will build solid partnerships across Product, Engineering, Support, Sales and business teams to connect customer and operational needs with engineering priorities. You will guide the design and delivery of secure, reliable services, automation and responsible AI capabilities, while ensuring that customer feedback and service insights influence product and engineering investment. 

Success in this role requires broad business and technical judgement, solid execution, and the ability to develop engineers who can operate across technical support, software and service engineering, reliability, automation, AI and security. The Voice of the Customer will remain central to prioritisation, service improvement and product influence. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organisation on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realise our shared goals. Each day, we build on our values of respect, integrity and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

Starting January 26, 2026, Microsoft AI (MAI) employees who live within a 50- mile commute of a designated Microsoft office in the U.S. or 25-mile commute of a non-U.S., country-specific location are expected to work from the office at least four days per week. This expectation is subject to local law and may vary by jurisdiction.



Responsibilities
  • Lead, coach and develop the team: Lead a team of Service and Automation Engineers, set clear priorities and outcomes, build technical capability, and create an inclusive environment where people can grow. 
  • Provide technical direction: Guide the design and delivery of scalable, secure and reliable services, automation and engineering solutions using technologies such as C#, .NET and Microsoft Azure. Support sound technical decisions through design reviews, technical proposals and targeted prototypes, while empowering engineers to own implementation and delivery. 
  • Own service health and operational performance: Ensure the team has the processes, tools and technical readiness required to provide reliable services and meet customer and business expectations. Use service signals and engineering data to identify risk, remove friction and prioritise improvement work. 
  • Build solid partnerships: Partner across Product, Engineering, Support, Sales and business teams to connect customer and operational needs with engineering priorities, align on trade-offs and deliver end-to-end solutions. 
  • Advocate for customers: Use customer feedback, support insights and service data to identify systemic issues, influence product and engineering investment, and ensure the Voice of the Customer is represented in technical priorities and decisions. 
  • Translate operational needs into engineering work: Work with Support and Operations teams to understand customer-impacting issues and recurring pain points, clarify requirements, and convert those insights into prioritised engineering work and product improvements. 
  • Lead incident management and prevention: Guide the response to significant service incidents, communicate customer and business impact clearly, drive effective root-cause analysis, and ensure post-incident learning results in durable corrective actions that reduce recurrence. 
  • Drive automation and self-service: Lead the development of automation, diagnostics, preventative guardrails and self-service capabilities that improve reliability, simplify operational processes, reduce manual effort and create reusable solutions. 
  • Guide responsible AI adoption: Provide direction for the development and adoption of AI-powered capabilities, including copilots, large language model integrations and agent-based workflows, with appropriate evaluation, security, safety and monitoring. 
  • Use data to guide investment and measure impact: Combine customer feedback, operational data, service trends and incident learning to identify priorities, evaluate outcomes and measure the customer and business impact of engineering improvements. 
  • Raise engineering standards: Promote high standards across quality, reliability, security, privacy and responsible engineering, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning and inclusion. 
  • Protect customers and the marketplace: Guide the use of advertiser, publisher, campaign and domain signals to identify patterns, safeguard advertiser return on investment, support user safety, and help detect fraudulent traffic and advertising practices. 
  • Manage suppliers where applicable: Set clear expectations for third-party vendors and service providers, monitor performance against service-level and contractual commitments, and address delivery or quality gaps.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Data Science, Cybersecurity, or related field AND technical experience in software engineering, network engineering, service engineering, systems engineering, or industrial controls
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • People management and/or technical leadership experience. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Data Science, Cybersecurity, or related field AND technical experience in software engineering, network engineering, service engineering, systems engineering, or industrial controls
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Data Science, Cybersecurity, or related field AND technical experience in software engineering, network engineering, service engineering, systems engineering, or industrial controls
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Experience in customer service, technical support, live-site operations or operational excellence. 
  • Experience leading teams through ambiguous, cross-functional technical work and taking ownership of complex problems. 
  • Working knowledge of software engineering and automation, including experience with one or more languages such as Python, C# or JavaScript, or equivalent scripting and development experience. 
  • Experience leading a software engineering, service engineering, site reliability or automation team in a production environment. 
  • Knowledge of digital advertising technologies and industry trends across search, display, native or video advertising. Experience partnering with Sales, Client Services, Support, Legal, Marketing, Security, Product and Engineering teams. 
  • Understanding of the software development lifecycle, agile delivery practices, technical design reviews, source control, testing, deployment and ongoing service ownership. 
  • Demonstrated experience in an engineering management role, including leading, coaching, and scaling engineering teams responsible for delivering high‑quality, reliable software.
  • Proven ability to lead multi‑team initiatives, operate effectively in ambiguous problem spaces, and influence outcomes across organizational boundaries.
  • Demonstrated track record of developing engineers and leaders, and of fostering inclusive, high‑performing engineering cultures focused on quality, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Experience applying automation, AI or Copilot capabilities to operational workflows, with attention to evaluation, adoption, measurement, security and responsible use. 
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues, customer impact, risk and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

We are recruiting outstanding Research Interns to work on autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI! Intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and safely interact with people and the physical world are rapidly becoming a reality. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments.

For example, how can we:

  • Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop?

  • Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications?

  • Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments?

  • Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents?

These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI.

  • Conducting original research and publishing your results.

  • Collaborating with research colleagues, internal product teams, and external researchers.

  • Transferring technology you’ve developed to relevant product groups.

What we need to see:

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

  • Relevant research experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, or autonomous systems.

  • Strong knowledge of the theory and practice of vehicle or robot autonomy—or expertise in a related area, with a strong interest in applying your work to autonomous systems.

  • A track record of research excellence, demonstrated through publications at leading conferences and journals—such as RSS, ICRA, CoRL, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc.—and through other research artifacts such as open-source software.

  • Exceptional Python programming skills; experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.

  • Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required, along with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, research-focused team.

Engineers on the Polaris team design tasks that test Gemini’s ability to complete software engineering work. A task is essentially an in-depth examination that evaluates how well Gemini performs in a specific, complex scenario. The primary components of a task are: a prompt that instructs Gemini what to do and a grader or rubric that assigns a numerical score to the model’s attempted solution.

Our team, Polaris, is distinguished primarily by how much manual effort we put into building individual tasks. Rather than generating a large number of tasks using a synthetic data pipeline, engineers on the Polaris team prioritize creating a smaller number of tasks that more closely capture the realism and complexity of real-world software engineering. A single well-designed task typically takes a Polaris engineer roughly one week to complete, from the initial ideation stage to final approval.

We're looking for a Senior SRE to own and scale the Kubernetes platform that assists NVIDIA's chip design (EDA) workloads. This is not a generic container-platform role. You'll be running Kubernetes at the edges of what it was developed for: orchestrating enormous stateful jobs, license-constrained EDA tooling, latency-sensitive access to high-performance shared storage, and tenants whose tapeout schedules do not move. The clusters you run sit alongside some of the largest EDA compute farms in the industry, spanning multiple on-prem datacenters and multiple public clouds. When these clusters degrade, chip schedules feel it - which is exactly what makes the reliability work exciting.

What you'll be doing:

  • Own Kubernetes clusters end-to-end - plan, deliver, upgrade, day-2 operations, and decommission - across on-prem datacenters and managed cloud Kubernetes (e.g. EKS, GKE, RKE, Red Hat OpenShift, etc.).
  • Define and implement the multi-cluster lifecycle strategy: version skew policy, patch cadence, node image pipelines, controlled rollouts, and safe upgrade mechanics for clusters that can't simply be drained on demand.
  • Treat on-prem and CSP Kubernetes as one platform with consistent APIs, policy, and observability - not as two disconnected worlds.
  • Drive everything through Infrastructure-as-Code, GitOps, and declarative config; manual cluster changes should be an anomaly worth investigating.
  • Design for failure: explicit fault domains, blast-radius containment between clusters and tenants, progressive delivery, and disciplined change control.
  • Build end-to-end observability (metrics, logs, traces, events) and push toward data-driven and auto-healing operations that materially reduce human intervention.
  • Participate in on-call, lead incident response, drive root cause analysis, and publish high-quality RCAs that actually change the system.
  • Partner with EDA engineering, storage, and network teams to land changes cleanly in a fast-moving environment.
  • Engage and partner with data center operations to help forecast, design and implement the accurate on-prem and cloud deployments to meet architectural needs.
  • Interface directly with internal EDA tenants/engineering teams  to design and implement operational improvements to increase productivity and provide faster and more reliable outcomes as well as partner with the infrastructure services team to help architect the supporting  capabilities for intelligent workload routing, observability, dynamic scaling and resource governance.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related technical field (or equivalent experience) with 8+ years building and supporting critical production services.
  • Deep, hands-on Kubernetes operations experience - you've run it, not just consumed it. Comfortable debugging etcd, kubelet, CNI, CSI, scheduler behavior, API server load, container runtime, and control-plane degradation under real production pressure.
  • Production experience with CSP-managed Kubernetes — including its upgrade model, networking and IAM integration, node group lifecycle, and where the managed abstraction stops helping you.
  • Production experience operating self-managed Kubernetes on-premises across multiple datacenters — cluster bring-up, bare-metal and GPU node lifecycle, multi-site topology, and the failure modes that only show up when you own the whole stack.
  • Strong command of CI/CD and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD/Flux or equivalents).
  • Demonstrated experience building large-scale infrastructure platforms for automated host lifecycle management, fleet reliability and auto-healing, end-to-end observability, or data-driven operations (AIOps/ML-driven signals) that measurably reduced toil.
  • Proficiency with monitoring, metrics,, and log collection tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Loki/ELK, containerd, etc.).
  • 5+ years of coding/scripting focusing on automation and operational management at scale in at least two languages such as Go, Python, Perl, or Ruby - with Go a strong plus for controller and operator work.
  • Track record mentoring engineers and influencing technical direction through design reviews, architecture documents, and strong partnership with team members and leadership.
  • Creative problem solver with excellent debugging instincts and strong written communication.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

Meta is seeking a Planning & Capacity Engineer to join the Capacity Planning & Delivery team to focus on planning optimization for Meta’s server and network rack supply chain. This role will focus on creating and optimizing supply chain plans at various altitudes to balance capacity, flexibility, supply capability, and cost, from base components to finished goods, in an environment of continual product introduction, directly managing billions of investments annually. We will do this primarily by building software and mathematical optimization models. The team is uniquely positioned to develop and optimize these capacity plans and scalably manage exceptions at the most strategic levels with company-level impact. This role is cross-functional and provides an opportunity to work with a variety of engineering and business teams to power the rapid growth of Meta’s products. This role will help to ensure optimal deployment and operation of our infrastructure from both a cost and a technological perspective, with millions of servers, gigawatts of data center capacity, and cutting-edge technology including advanced AI.

Responsibilities

  • Own infrastructure supply chain planning for Meta (as part of Meta’s overall capacity plan) across all components of server and network racks
  • Design improvements to software systems to improve supply chain planning efficiency and quality, partner with software engineers to implement and contribute code yourself
  • Develop and analyze business and technical data and scenarios to drive executive decisions around infrastructure supply and spend
  • Contribute to end to end supply chain planning processes (as part of Meta’s overall capacity plan), methodologies, and data to deliver an executable and optimized supply plan
  • Manage and resolve critical escalations and exceptions in all areas of the supply chain
  • Develop models that drive supply flexibility and optionality to best balance the delivery of required capacity, cost, and risk
  • Build mathematical models to perform simulations and optimization studies of demand projections, scenario planning, and gap closure analysis while balancing constraints, product mix, and inventory costs
  • Work cross-functionally to define problem statements, collect data, build analytical models, and make recommendations to drive change and optimization at the most strategic levels
  • Partner across Infra - platform teams, server hardware engineering, network engineering, data center engineering, operations, capacity planning, networking planning, data center planning, energy - to find the most optimal ways to build and scale our infrastructure
  • Partner with Finance to balance cost efficiency with technical, product, and supply chain considerations
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to a team of commodity planners

  • 8+ years of experience in coding/scripting languages such as Python, R, Java, C, C++, PHP

  • Experience defining project scope, priorities, and next steps when requirements or constraints are not fully defined

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience redesigning or replacing business planning systems or models that resulted in measurable improvements to planning accuracy, efficiency, or cost outcomes
  • Track record of success in planning for a complex supply chain environment
  • Experience identifying process improvements or novel approaches that resulted in measurable gains in efficiency, cost savings, or capacity outcomes

Come and develop, drive, and deliver new products in the world of Meta's Reality Labs! We're looking for individuals that want to be on the ground floor of breakthrough technologies and help build a high-performing sourcing team. As a Strategic Sourcing Manager (SSM), you will be responsible for developing the key strategic relationships and sourcing strategies for camera, depth, and optics modules and their critical components—including (but not limited to) camera modules, depth/ToF modules, structured light components, lenses, lens barrels, actuators (AF/OIS), optical filters, VCSEL/laser emitters, receivers, flexes/connectors, and module-level integration partners. You will lead commercial negotiations, part/module costing (BOM and conversion), and end-to-end supply chain management. This role depends on close collaboration with Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Camera/Depth Systems teams, Program Management, Quality, and Supplier development Engineers. During the product development process, you are responsible for ensuring suppliers are prepared to support delivery of modules and key parts on-time at specified quality, reliability, yield, and performance parameters, and are prepared to meet ramp quantities. It is the SSM's primary objective to ensure suppliers meet commercial and technical requirements throughout the life-cycle of the product(s).

Responsibilities

  • Help support the development of commodity/category sourcing strategies for Camera, Depth, and Optics modules, ensuring suppliers can meet Smartglasses/AR current and future technical and business requirements
  • Be a subject matter expert in module integration supply chains (camera/depth modules), including key manufacturing processes, capacity models, yield drivers, test coverage, and reliability requirements
  • Continually benchmark the industry to monitor technology trends (camera sensors and module architectures, depth modalities, lens and coating technologies, actuator trends, optical safety/regulatory requirements) and ensure best practices are incorporated into the Reality Labs supply chain
  • Lead supplier selection criteria, evaluate alternative suppliers, manage RFQs, and drive final supplier selection in partnership with Engineering, Quality, and Technical Operations
  • Drive end-to-end module commercial ownership, including BOM cost, conversion cost, labor/overhead, yield assumptions, tooling/NRE, and cost-down roadmaps
  • Formulate contingency plans to de-risk technical challenges, long lead times, single-source dependencies, cost challenges, and any supply issues (multi-site, alternate process flows, buffer strategies)
  • Institute checks and balances to optimize schedule flexibility while minimizing excess inventory exposure (E&O risk management, hubbing strategy, VMI/consignment where applicable)
  • Partner with CMs/ODMs/EMS and module integrators to resolve part shortages, quality issues, or yield excursions that impact production schedules; drive rapid containment and recovery plans
  • Own ramp readiness including risk buys, capacity bring-up, line qualification, and supply assurance plans to support production plan and forecasts for designated suppliers
  • Lead supplier development agreements to onboard new module integrators and key optical component suppliers; ensure qualification plans (FAI/PPAP-like readiness, GR&R, reliability) are agreed and executed
  • Close Statements of Work (SOW) for new projects covering tooling, automation, EVT/DVT/PVT builds, characterization, reliability testing, and failure analysis support
  • Influence supplier technology roadmaps and create internal disruptive value-add to ensure Meta's system architecture and commercial requirements are met (size, weight, power, performance, reliability, and cost)
  • Establish and manage strategic supplier relationships at the executive level; lead QBRs, escalation paths, and long-term partnership planning

Minimum Qualifications

  • BS degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or relevant field
  • 10+ years of work experience in sourcing or related fields associated with camera/depth modules, optics components, consumer electronics modules, or adjacent electromechanical supply chains
  • Strong experience in module integration management: supplier evaluation/selection, RFQ execution, cost modeling (BOM + conversion), contract negotiation, and supplier performance management
  • Experience driving cross-functional execution with Engineering, Quality, Ops/Manufacturing, and Program Management across development builds and ramp
  • Material management and CTB (Clear to Build) proficiency; ability to manage lead times, allocation risk, and build readiness
  • Experience communicating with and influencing all levels of management

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience sourcing and managing suppliers for optical components (lenses, coatings, filters, actuators, VCSEL/laser, receivers) and/or camera/depth module integrators
  • Optical understanding is preferred (imaging or depth fundamentals, key optical performance drivers), but not required
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience with high volume consumer electronics products and global manufacturing ecosystems
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • 10+ years of sourcing experience managing global suppliers across module integrators and critical component ecosystems
